extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and third-party reexamination requesters (patent practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing ex parte reexamination of U.S. patents, including what submissions will be considered, scope of reexamination, prior art treatment, timing, service, and examiner responsibilities. Targets examiners and practitioners handling reexamination orders, statements, and replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on further papers by third party requester
rubrics_metrics.description: The third party requester is not permitted to file any further papers after his or her reply to the patent owner’s statement; any further papers will not be considered and will be returned to the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The active participation of the ex parte reexamination requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535; no further submissions on behalf of the requester will be acknowledged or considered. The patent owner cannot file papers on behalf of the requester to circumvent the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely filing/consideration of statement and reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file or serve the documents set forth in § 1.530 or § 1.535 may result in their being refused consideration; no submissions other than the statement (§ 1.530) and the requester’s reply (§ 1.535) will be considered prior to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although § 1.540 uses discretionary language, patent owners and requesters can expect untimely statement/reply to be refused consideration; untimely submissions ordinarily not considered or placed on record (except some untimely owner papers after response period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service required
rubrics_metrics.description: Any paper for which proof of service is required that is filed without proof of service may be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no proof of service is included, reexamination clerk should inquire of the sender whether service was made; if no service was made, paper is placed in file but not considered. See MPEP § 2266.03 and § 2267.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner will consider properly filed submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once reexamination is ordered, any submissions properly filed and served in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530 and 1.535 will be considered by the examiner when preparing the first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of proposed amendments guided by 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); consideration of patent owner’s statement guided by 1.530(c); consideration of requester’s reply guided by 1.535.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of issues raised in requester’s reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requester’s reply raises issues not previously presented, such issues will be treated by the examiner in the Office action if they are within the scope of reexamination; issues not within scope should be treated pursuant to 37 CFR 1.552(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems outside the permitted scope should be noted and not resolved in reexamination; patent owner may consider reissue to resolve such issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of new matter in reexamination is governed by MPEP § 2270.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New or amended subject matter is examined under 35 U.S.C. 112 requirements; see MPEP § 2270 for rules on entry and treatment of new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings conducted with special dispatch and per examination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After times for filing statement and reply have expired, reexamination is conducted according to procedures for initial examination (sections 132 and 133) and shall be conducted with special dispatch within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.550(a): examination follows §§ 1.104–1.116 and results in issuance of an ex parte reexamination certificate under § 1.570; full search not routinely made by examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner allowed to amend but cannot enlarge claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner will be permitted to propose any amendment and new claims to distinguish the invention from cited prior art or in response to an adverse decision, but no proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of a claim will be permitted in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses to rejections may include further statements and/or proposed amendments/new claims to place patent in a condition where all claims, if amended as proposed, would be patentable. Examiners ensure amendments do not enlarge scope (35 U.S.C. 305).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time only for sufficient cause with petition fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Time for action by a patent owner in ex parte reexamination will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; any request for extension must be filed on or before the due date and must be accompanied by the petition fee in § 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere filing of a request does not effect an extension; see § 1.304(a) for extensions relating to appeals/ civil actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of prosecution for failure to timely respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action or any written statement of an interview required under § 1.560(b), the prosecution in the ex parte reexamination proceeding will be a terminated prosecution and the Director will proceed to issue and publish a certificate concluding the reexamination proceeding under § 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.550(d) for termination rule and issuance of certificate in accordance with last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excusing delay: unavoidable vs unintentional
rubrics_metrics.description: If a response is not timely filed, the delay may be excused if shown unavoidable (petition under § 1.137(a)), or the response may be accepted if the delay was unintentional (petition under § 1.137(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must comply with § 1.137 requirements and be timely filed; supporting evidence required per petition type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirement after filing reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for ex parte reexamination, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on the other party in the manner provided by § 1.248; the document must reflect service or it may be refused consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents lacking proper service can be refused; reexamination requester will be sent copies of Office actions issued during proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions after order and entry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No further active participation by a third party requester is allowed once ex parte reexamination is ordered and response times have expired; no third party submissions will be acknowledged or considered unless they are in accordance with 37 CFR 1.510/1.535 or were entered in the patent file prior to the order under § 1.525.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions by third parties filed after date of order must meet requirements of and will be treated in accordance with § 1.501(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner cannot file papers prepared by third party to circumvent ex parte rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may not file papers on behalf of the requester and thereby circumvent the intent of the ex parte reexamination legislation and the rules; papers prepared by a third party and filed by the patent owner will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court cannot order a patent owner to file papers prepared by third party in addition to owner’s own submission (Emerson Elec. Co. v. Davoil). Such filings will be returned as inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who conducts the examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination will ordinarily be conducted by the same patent examiner who made the decision on whether the reexamination request should be granted, but if a petition under 37 CFR 1.515(c) is granted, the reexamination will normally be conducted by another examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2236 and § 2248 for petition/change procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary sources of prior art to be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, primary source of prior art are the patents and printed publications cited in the request for ex parte reexamination; examiner must also consider patents and printed publications cited by others, cited in owner’s statement or requester’s reply if complying with 1.98, cited under duty of disclosure, discovered by examiner, of record from earlier examination, and of record from any 1.501 submission prior to the order if complying with 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated as items (A)–(F). Examiner consideration of submitted items is normally limited by the degree to which the submitting party explained content and relevance. Examiner initials on citation forms do not imply more consideration than indicated in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of consideration depends on explanation of relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where patents/publications are submitted in compliance with rules, the degree of consideration is normally limited by the degree to which the submitting party explained the content and relevance of the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner initials adjacent to citations on PTO forms do not signify further consideration beyond what is noted in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit reference copies per 37 CFR 1.98
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2) requires a legible copy of each foreign patent, each publication or that portion which caused it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required), for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application the specification including claims and drawings or the portion which caused listing, and all other information or that portion which caused listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception in 1.98(d)(1) does not apply to reexamination proceedings (they do not receive 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit). Submissions not complying may be returned/expunged/discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on submitting copending reexaminations/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not required nor permitted to submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings and applications (which can be mistaken for a new request/filing); submitters may provide the application/proceeding number and its status instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorised submissions will be returned, expunged, or discarded at Office discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late submissions after Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the NIRC has been mailed, if the patent owner provides a submission of patents/printed publications or other 1.98(a) information after NIRC, the submission must be accompanied by (A) a factual accounting explaining why it could not have been submitted earlier and (B) an explanation of relevance to the claimed invention; entry requires a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 (with fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement (B) is to facilitate Office compliance with statutory 'special dispatch'; petitions must show the requisite grounds to interrupt proceeding after NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions during printing cycle require stringent showing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission is made while a proceeding is in its 'printing cycle' (post-NIRC), the patent owner must provide an unequivocal statement that at least one claim is unpatentable, an amendment to such claim(s), and an explanation how the amendment makes the claim(s) patentable, in addition to the factual accounting; entry also requires a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal from printing cycle is burdensome; petition must provide the showing discussed to justify interruption of printing cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of prior art on specified forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination request must provide a listing of the patents and printed publications as provided in 37 CFR 1.98; the examiner must list on form PTO-892 (or equivalent) all prior art patents/printed publications cited in the decision, applied in making rejections, or cited as pertinent during reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All citations listed on PTO-892 and all citations not lined-through on forms PTO/SB/08A/08B/PTO/SB/42 (or equivalents) will be printed on the reexamination certificate under 'References Cited.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to entry and citation in reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission of patents and/or publications is entitled to entry and citation in the reexamination certificate when it complies with 37 CFR 1.98 and is submitted by (A) the patent owner in the statement under 1.530, (B) the requester in the reply under 1.535, (C) prior to the order under 1.501 by any party, and/or (D) by the patent owner under duty of disclosure 1.555.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and compliance with 1.98 are essential for inclusion in the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reexamination per 37 CFR 1.552
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in ex parte reexamination will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, with respect to subject matter added or deleted in the reexamination proceeding, on the basis of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112. Claims will not be permitted to enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent. Issues other than those indicated will not be resolved in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination provides complete reexamination of claims on prior art patents/printed publications; 35 U.S.C. 112 issues addressed only for new/amendatory subject matter. If other issues are raised, examiner notes them in next Office action and owner may consider reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections based only on patents and printed publications (35 U.S.C. 102/103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections on prior art in reexamination proceedings may only be made on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications and may be based upon appropriate portions of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections cannot be based on matters other than patents/printed publications (e.g., public use or sale, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 101, conduct issues). Prior art must be applied under appropriate statutory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening patents/printed publications as prior art when effective date limits apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections may be made based on intervening patents or printed publications where the patent claims under reexamination are entitled only to the filing date of the patent and are not supported by an earlier foreign or U.S. patent application whose filing date is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In re Ruscetta, In re van Langenhoven cited; see MPEP § 201.11 for details on effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting is proper consideration in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting is appropriate for consideration in reexamination both as a basis for ordering reexamination and during examination on the merits; the examiner should determine whether the issue raises a substantial new question of patentability and whether a double patenting rejection is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double patenting may be overcome by terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(c)/(d); where present may arise from same inventive entity, different entities with common inventor, common assignee, or joint research agreement activities (enumerated A–D). Special rules apply post-2004 and under CREATE Act; see MPEP §§ 804 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations only to explain contents/dates of prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations or other written evidence that explain contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications may be considered, but any rejection must be based upon the prior art patents or printed publications as explained; the rejection cannot be based on the affidavits/declarations themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits can clarify prior art but cannot constitute independent basis for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of admissions by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions by the patent owner of record in the file or in a court record may be utilized in combination with a patent or printed publication to determine scope and content of prior art in reexamination; an admission is treated as prior art evidence and requires no independent proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions can be in the file history or presented during reexamination or litigation; third parties may not submit admissions of the patent owner made outside the file or court record. Initial reexamination consideration under 35 U.S.C. 303 is limited to patents/printed publications, so admissions per se may not establish substantial new question pre-order but can be used post-order in conjunction with patents/publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation limited to patents/printed publications under proper 35 U.S.C. provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claims will be examined only on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications applied under the appropriate parts of 35 U.S.C. 102 (and 103 as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner applies statutory provisions when interpreting and applying prior art to claims; admissions and affidavits are used only as explained above.
